memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Israelites travelled to the plains of Moab and camped along the Jordan across from Jericho. Now Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites, and Moab was terrified because there were so many people. Indeed, Moab was filled with dread because of the Israelites. - Num 22:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Israel arrives at the plains of Moab, camped and waiting across from Jericho. They have done nothing to threaten Moab, yet a wave of terror sweeps over the land. Balak, the Moabite king, watches this great multitude and is filled with dread.

Notice that Israel had not attacked Moab. Their reputation alone, and the memory of what God had done through them, was enough to make a king tremble. Fear has a way of magnifying threats that are not even there. Balak saw danger where God had actually commanded restraint toward Moab.

There is something to learn here about the fear that grips the human heart. When we forget God, even imagined threats can overwhelm us. Balak did not know the living God, so he had no anchor for his soul. His fear drove him toward desperate and foolish decisions, as the rest of the chapter will show.

How different it is for those who know the Lord. The same God whose presence made kings tremble is the God who tells His people, again and again, not to be afraid. In Christ we need not be ruled by dread, for perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). Whose presence shapes your response to what you cannot control?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What imagined fears have driven you toward foolish decisions?
2. Do you face uncertainty with dread or with trust in God?
3. How does knowing the Lord steady your heart in fearful times?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when fear tempts me to see danger everywhere, anchor my heart in You. Free me from dread, for Your perfect love casts out all fear. Amen.
